  <bpmn:process id="Process_ClaimHandling" name="Claim Review Process" isExecutable="false">
    <bpmn:laneSet id="LaneSet_ClaimReview">
      <bpmn:lane id="Lane_ClaimsOfficer" name="Claims Officer">
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>StartEvent_ClaimRegistered</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_ExamineClaim</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_WriteRecommendation</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
      </bpmn:lane>
      <bpmn:lane id="Lane_SeniorClaimsOfficer" name="Senior Claims Officer">
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Task_CheckRecommendation</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>Gateway_ClaimDecision</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
        <bpmn:flowNodeRef>EndEvent_ClaimOK</bpmn:flowNodeRef>
      </bpmn:lane>
    </bpmn:laneSet>

    <bpmn:startEvent id="StartEvent_ClaimRegistered" name="Claim registered">
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_RegisteredToExamine</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:startEvent>

    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_ExamineClaim" name="Examine claim">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_RegisteredToExamine</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_ExamineToWrite</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:userTask>

    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_WriteRecommendation" name="Write settlement recommendation">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_ExamineToWrite</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_NotOKToWrite</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_WriteToCheck</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:userTask>

    <bpmn:userTask id="Task_CheckRecommendation" name="Check settlement recommendation">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_WriteToCheck</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_CheckToDecision</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:userTask>

    <bpmn:exclusiveGateway id="Gateway_ClaimDecision" name="Claim marked OK or Not OK?">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_CheckToDecision</bpmn:incoming>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_OK</bpmn:outgoing>
      <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_NotOK</bpmn:outgoing>
    </bpmn:exclusiveGateway>

    <bpmn:endEvent id="EndEvent_ClaimOK" name="Claim marked OK, claim handling proceeds">
      <bpmn:incoming>Flow_OK</bpmn:incoming>
    </bpmn:endEvent>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_RegisteredToExamine" sourceRef="StartEvent_ClaimRegistered" targetRef="Task_ExamineClaim"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_ExamineToWrite" sourceRef="Task_ExamineClaim" targetRef="Task_WriteRecommendation"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_WriteToCheck" sourceRef="Task_WriteRecommendation" targetRef="Task_CheckRecommendation"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_CheckToDecision" sourceRef="Task_CheckRecommendation" targetRef="Gateway_ClaimDecision"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_OK" name="OK" sourceRef="Gateway_ClaimDecision" targetRef="EndEvent_ClaimOK">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">OK</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_NotOK" name="Not OK" sourceRef="Gateway_ClaimDecision" targetRef="Task_WriteRecommendation">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">Not OK</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
  </bpmn:process>
</bpmn:definitions>

rules.instruction: When the description states that a reviewer may either approve an item or send it back, and that a returned item is first changed by a stated action and then submitted again to the same reviewer, so that the revision path contains two separately described actions before the review is repeated: Model the reviewer's approval as its own task performed by that reviewer, not only as a gateway flow label. On the return branch, model the change action and the resubmission action as separate tasks, in that order, connected by sequence flows. Then connect the resubmission task to the merge gateway that leads back into the review, so that neither action is folded into the other or into the gateway.
rules.situation: the description says that an output is checked by a reviewer, who then marks it with one of two outcomes (for example OK or Not OK), and each outcome has its own stated follow-up action

rules.instruction: When the description states that a review or assessment by one party leads to an approval, that the approval itself is performed work by that party, and that the approved outcome is then carried out through several separately described actions (for example, one that changes duties and another that changes pay), each given its own sentence: Model the approval as its own task performed by the stated party, placed after the review and before the approved branch. Then model each separately described follow-up action as its own task, in the order or concurrency the description gives, after the approval. Do not leave the approval implicit in the gateway label, and do not merge the follow-up actions into one combined task.
rules.situation: the description states a sequence of actions, each performed by a named role, and a later action by another role decides whether the earlier result is accepted or sent back

rules.instruction: When The description states a chain of activities in which each sentence introduces the next activity, some phrased passively or as a hand-off to another party (for example 'is examined by', 'then writes', 'is then checked by'), and then a checking party records one of two verdicts that either sends the work back to an earlier party or lets the process continue.: Model every stated activity in the chain, including passive or hand-off activities, as its own task in sequence, placed in the lane of the party that performs it. Model the checking step as its own task performed by the checking party, placed after the last task of the chain and before a verdict gateway. Place an exclusive gateway after that checking task with one conditioned outgoing flow per verdict. On the return branch, model the stated return as its own task performed by the party named in the description, and connect it back to the earlier stated activity so that the loop is visible. On the continuation branch, model the stated continuation as a task or as a flow into the next activity, and do not replace it with an end event unless the description says the process ends there.
rules.situation: The description states a chain of activities in which each sentence introduces the next activity, some phrased passively or as a hand-off to another party (for example 'is examined by', 'then writes', 'is then checked by'), and then a checking party records one of two verdicts that either sends the work back to an earlier party or lets the process continue.

rules.instruction: When the description states a chain of activities in which each sentence introduces the next activity, some phrased passively or as a hand-off to another party, and then a party records one of two outcomes that either sends the work back to an earlier party or lets the process continue.: Model every stated activity in the chain, including passive or hand-off activities, as its own task in sequence, placed in the lane of the party that performs it. Model the checking step as its own task performed by the party that records the outcome, placed after the last task of the chain and before an exclusive gateway. Give that gateway one conditioned outgoing flow per outcome. On the return branch, model the stated return as its own task performed by the party named in the description, and connect it back to the earlier stated activity so the loop is visible. On the continuation branch, model the stated continuation as a task or as a flow into the next activity, and do not replace it with an end event unless the description says the process ends there.
rules.situation: the description states that a produced result is handed over to a different party for checking, phrased as a passive sentence (for example 'is then checked by'), and that party then records a decision that is either OK or Not OK
